name: St. Jakob in Defereggen
kurzbeschreibung: Charming main town of the Defereggental, featuring a beautiful church and a summer sledging run.
beschreibung:
Overview

St. Jakob in Defereggen is situated at an elevation of 1,389 meters in the upper Defereggental valley in East Tyrol’s Lienz district, framed by the soaring 3,000-meter peaks of the Rieserferner Group to the south and the Venediger Group to the north. Home to roughly 850 residents, the municipality lies within the Hohe Tauern National Park, extending west to the Staller Sattel mountain pass (2,052 m) on the Italian South Tyrolean border. Celebrated for its low-allergen curative climate, pristine larch forests, and crystal-clear mountain streams, St. Jakob preserves a 500-year mining legacy, historic alpine dairy farming, certified healing mineral springs, and a snow-sure family ski domain reaching 2,525 meters far from the crowds.

History

Prehistoric artifacts demonstrate that passes like Staller Sattel and Klammljoch were traversed since the Stone Age. The valley's oldest documented settlement is the Jagdhausalm, recorded in 1212 as a permanent medieval dairy estate. St. Jakob’s church was first cited in 1299. The village prospered as East Tyrol’s oldest mining settlement: from the early 16th century, high-altitude silver, lead, and copper lodes were worked in the Trojertal valley, leading to the construction of a major smelting works and stamp mill in 1617. A cultural marvel is the Jagdhausalm at 2,009 meters: recognized as Austria's oldest alpine pasture village, its cluster of 15 stone farmhouses and chapel earned it the moniker Little Tibet of the Alps, held for centuries by South Tyrolean graziers. The neoclassical parish church of Saint James the Greater was constructed between 1827 and 1831 by architect Simon Moosbrugger, adorned with frescoes by Johann Baptist Oberkofler.

Getting there

St. Jakob in Defereggen is reached via scenic alpine routes. From northern Austria and Germany, travel via Mittersill through the Felbertauern Tunnel (B108 toll road) to Matrei in Osttirol, turning at Huben onto the L25 Defereggental road for 25 kilometers directly into St. Jakob. From the south or east, arrive via Lienz along the B108. In summer (June to October), a scenic direct connection links South Tyrol through the Antholz Valley over the Staller Sattel pass (2,052 m, regulated by single-lane timed traffic lights). Train travelers arrive at Lienz railway station, connecting to regular VVT bus line 953 running straight into Defereggental.

Tips

Journey to the remote Jagdhausalm at 2,009 meters in the Schwarzachtal valley to marvel at Austria’s oldest stone hamlet, evocative of a Himalayan settlement within Hohe Tauern National Park. At the Staller Sattel pass, stroll around emerald Lake Obersee surrounded by rocky summits. In winter, the Brunnalm ski area provides 17 kilometers of uncrowded slopes ascending to 2,525 meters. Discover the Deferegger Healing Waters center, drawing fossil iodine-rich thermal brine from ancient seas 1,850 meters underground. Nature lovers should also explore the Oberhauser Stone Pine Forest, the largest contiguous Swiss pine woodland in the Eastern Alps, featuring an interpretive trail and viewing tower.
